name: What is the difference between installing a kitchen peninsula and an island?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between installing a kitchen peninsula and an island?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Use a peninsula when you want attached storage and counter space; choose a freestanding island when the room supports circulation around all sides and you want a central work zone. Neither option is automatically better.

Context: A peninsula commonly uses the wall or existing cabinet run for support and utility access, while an island needs independent support and may require floor-based utility routes. The choice should follow the room’s dimensions and work pattern.

Key factors:
- Room width and aisle clearances
- Number of traffic paths
- Utility relocation needs
- Seating and prep priorities

Practical guidance: Compare both options on the same scaled plan with appliance doors, stools, and open drawers shown. Include the cost of demolition and utility changes, not only cabinets and countertop.

Elite Remodeling & Design can develop alternative kitchen layouts before construction decisions are finalized.
acceptedAnswer.description: A peninsula attaches to a wall or cabinet run and usually needs less independent support and fewer floor utility changes. An island offers access from all sides but needs more clearance. Compare both layouts with real appliances, stools, and traffic paths shown.
